limitations: No Digital Macaroni hands-on workspace design, migration, automation, permission, or support test was completed.
Dated complaints were not repeated as current facts without fresh confirmation.
A configurable workspace succeeds or fails partly on the system the buyer designs inside it.

claims.statement: Fibery is a configurable workspace that connects databases, documents, whiteboards, views, automations, and integrations.
Free supports up to ten users and ten databases. Annual prices are €12 per user for Standard, €20 for Pro, and €40 for Enterprise; observers and guests are free on paid plans.
Linked data, adaptable workflows, connected information, and replacing narrower tools are the strongest repeated positives.
The flexibility creates a steep setup and learning cost because the team must design its own work system.
Reporting, external sharing, permission clarity, notifications, and resource planning appear as narrower weak points.
Support and the pace of product improvement receive repeated praise.

scoreRationale.onboarding: Templates help, but the real work is agreeing on types, links, names, views, and ownership.
scoreRationale.product: Excellent for connected work that does not fit a rigid tool; excessive for a simple task list.
scoreRationale.support: Customer service is a consistent strength in the available review pools.
scoreRationale.billing: The free tier is generous and paid observers and guests are free, but automation, sync, AI, history, and permission limits differ by plan.
scoreRationale.overall: Fibery is for teams willing to design a shared operating system. Prototype one cross-team workflow before moving everything.

conflictsAndUnknowns: The freedom users praise is the source of the setup cost they criticize.
Replacing several tools can reduce handoffs but makes workspace design and ownership more important.
No current mobile, report, permission, migration, performance, or support test was completed.
